newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba hosts leftist youth festival.
newsitem.headline: Cuba hosts leftist youth festival.

text.p: Cuba on Monday opened a gathering of 10,000 leftist youths and students from around the world, calling on them to join what it views as a fight for social justice and against U.S. imperialism.
"Ideas have no frontiers," Union of Young Communists leader Victoria Velazquez told a mass of flag-waving, cheering young people gathered at the steps of Havana University.

President Fidel Castro presided over the opening of the meeting, the first international leftist youth festival since North Korea hosted a meeting in 1989, before the collapse of communism in the former Soviet Union and eastern Europe.
Communist-ruled Cuba undertook two years ago to revive a faltering tradition of periodic leftist youth meetings that have been held since 1947.
The University walls, backdrop for a ceremony of speeches and songs, were decorated with a series of giant portraits of legendary revolutionary Ernesto "Che" Guevara.

Cuba has dedicated the festival to Guevara, the Argentine- born doctor who was Castro's right-hand man in his guerrilla war leading up to the 1959 revolution, and who inspired a generation of leftists around the world.
Cuba is seeking to show Guevara's revolutionary ideals are still valid, in particular for the youth of Cuba and abroad.

Guevara was killed in October 1967 while leading an abortive guerrilla uprising in Boliva. Two weeks ago, Guevara's remains were returned to Cuba after being unearthed from a secret mass grave in Bolivia.

The "14th World Festival of Youth and Students for anti- imperialist Solidarity, Peace and Friendship" will consist of nine days of political discussion groups, concerts and parties. Velazquez said delegates had come from 106 countries.
She said the largest single delegation was a group of more than 700 young people from the United States, who had defied U.S. travel restrictions in order to come to Cuba.

The U.S. delegation travelled despite the 35-year-old U.S. economic embargo on Cuba that includes restrictions on travel to Cuba by U.S. citizens. They were not given an official U.S. exemption for their trip and so travelled without permission, arriving mostly on charter flights from Cancun in Mexico and Nassau in the Bahamas.
Havana authorities have tried to present the run-down city in its best light, festooning main streets with flags and stepping up garbage collection.

Local authorities have provided Cuban families hosting the delegates with special packages of food and drink, including beer and rum, to offer to their guests. Without such help, it would be difficult for many Cubans to offer a guest a meal that included meat and beer.
